page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is a KVM-based virtual server configured with an Intel Xeon 8570 processor. It features 24 physical x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 10.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU containing 192 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across memory and compute operations. The system achieved a PassMark CPU score of 52754.5 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 47902.58. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4156.98 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 115.78 GB/sec. Large-scale data processing is supported by strong compression and decompression metrics, including a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 352.97 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier LLM inference capabilities, processing 9953.26 tokens per second for prompt processing and 525.92 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a massive 192 GB GPU frame buffer with 240 GB of system memory, making it highly optimized for memory-intensive parallel computing. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage represent notable architectural tradeoffs that require external storage solutions. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as large language model inference, deep learning training, high-performance database operations, and complex physics simulations.
